name: agent-fs-per-path-permission
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): the fs tools (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`) confine every operation to a path the acting agent is permitted to edit, delegating the per-path decision to opencode 2.x's permission engine through `ctx.permission.assert`.

An opencode 2.x tool executor is `execute(input, context)`, and `context` carries the caller identity — `context.agent` (the acting agent's ID), `context.sessionID`, `context.messageID`, and `context.id` — alongside `progress` and `signal`. Before touching a path the tool asserts the `edit` action with the RESOLVED target path as the resource:

`ctx.permission.assert({ sessionID: context.sessionID, agent: context.agent, action: "edit", resources: [<resolved target path>], source: { type: "tool", messageID: context.messageID, id: context.id }, save: [...] })`

opencode evaluates the acting agent's ordered rules for the `edit` action on that path — the lower-priority configuration first, the global rules next, the agent's own rules last, the LAST matching entry winning — resolves on allow, prompts on `ask`, and otherwise rejects. The asserted `agent` selects whose rules apply and defaults to the session's agent.

The tools are FAIL-CLOSED: a deny rule or a rejection with feedback rejects with a `Tool.Error` carrying the reason, which the tool lets propagate to the model; a plain rejection ends the current step; in every case the mutation does not proceed, and an unresolvable acting agent or path refuses. The tool-name action (`apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp`, resource `*`) is the CALLABILITY gate; the per-path scope comes from the `edit`-action assert with the resolved path as its resource. For the two-argument tools (`apg_mv`, `apg_cp`) both the source and the destination path are asserted; when one assert call carries multiple resources together — as these send the source and the destination — opencode resolves them as any deny denies, otherwise any ask asks, otherwise allowed. `external_directory` governs a path outside the active Location and its project worktree.

The fs scope tracks the effective `edit` scope, so a `deny` the `edit` action honours likewise refuses the fs operation. The boundary is the PROJECT WORKTREE: for a code-writer, a path that resolves into the main checkout (outside every project worktree) is refused regardless of the caller-supplied directory, and no operation crosses the project/worktree boundary. The capability is never granted as a blanket `"*": allow`: the grant is deny-by-default with the role's owned globs allowed under `apg/.worktrees/*/` only. The tools perform plain filesystem operations only — they are not `git rm`/`git mv` — and they never mutate graph nodes (that is `apg node rm` / `apg edge rm`).

This mechanism is the opencode 2.x plugin API's documented permission surface — the tool executor context's caller identity plus `ctx.permission.assert`. It is verified by unit/int tests against a faked V2 tool context carrying `agent`/`sessionID`/`messageID`/`id` and an assertable permission surface; verification against a live opencode 2.x runtime is outside the unit/int test tiers.
